name: Daycare, nurseries and preschools

problems.words: Our waitlist is in a notebook and we lose track of who's still interested
quick_ideas: Move the waitlist into one list by family reference, preferred start month and room, so it can be sorted
Contact each family once to confirm interest, using the number they gave with permission, so the list is real.

workzap_build.text: A waitlist and tour tracker with follow-up dates and offer status, reviewed each month across centres.

problems.ask_first: Of the families on the waitlist, are most still interested, or have you lost touch with most?
problems.free_stops: The waitlist stages and follow-up timing are kept for the document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many notebook entries have no recent contact note, so you can see how stale the waitlist really is.
Give one person the waitlist notebook and a fixed weekly review time, so follow-up stops getting missed between other jobs.

problems.words: Toddler room is full but preschool has empty places
quick_ideas: Write down places filled per room for the next few months, so upcoming gaps show early
Offer the coming gaps to waitlist families first, so places don't sit empty.

workzap_build.text: A room capacity board showing places filled against your licensed capacity per room, looking months ahead and updated daily.

problems.ask_first: Is the toddler room full all year, or only in certain months?
problems.free_stops: How room moves are forecast is in the document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare weekly enquiries for toddler places against empty preschool places this week, so you can judge the mismatch clearly.
Make one person review room availability with the enquiry notebook every Friday, so empty preschool places get offered sooner.

problems.words: Staff call in sick and we struggle to cover rooms that morning
quick_ideas: Ask staff to call in to one number by a fixed early time, so cover starts sooner
Keep a short list of on-call staff, so there is someone to ring first.

workzap_build.text: A roster planner showing staffing per room against expected attendance and your own ratio settings, with the cover list contacted when needed.

problems.ask_first: Do sick calls come mostly on certain days, or spread across the week?
problems.free_stops: The roster rules and cover order are kept for the document.

extra_ideas.text: Write down which rooms need last-minute cover most often this month, so the pressure points are clear before the next rota.
Give one supervisor the morning cover call job at a fixed time, so room cover starts earlier on sick days.

problems.words: Subsidy claims take me two evenings every month
quick_ideas: Total attendance days per room at the end of each day this month, so month-end is just adding up
For what the claim requires, check with your provincial programme contact, so the format is right.

workzap_build.text: Daily attendance counts put together into a claim workbook for you to check and submit.

problems.ask_first: Do the subsidy claim evenings go mostly on counting attendance, or on filling in the forms?
problems.free_stops: How the workbook is built to your province's format is in the document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare each room’s daily attendance mark with the final monthly claim line once this week, so the rework hotspot shows.
Give the closing supervisor one notebook page for room attendance totals each day, so claim figures are ready before month end.

problems.words: Subsidy payments come late and I'm short for payroll
quick_ideas: Write down when each payment usually arrives against payroll dates, so the gap is known
Talk to your accountant about how to cover it, so payroll isn't a surprise.

workzap_build.text: A cash view showing expected subsidy and parent payments against payroll and rent, updated daily.

problems.ask_first: Do subsidy payments arrive a few days late, or weeks late?
problems.free_stops: How the cash view is set up is kept for the document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many staff paydays passed before each subsidy payment reached you lately, so you can see the payroll squeeze length.
Give one person one notebook page for all expected subsidy dates and wage dates, so missed handovers stop causing payroll stress.

problems.words: Parents pay late and some leave owing two months
quick_ideas: List every account behind today, by family reference, so you see the total
Offer families a regular payment method such as pre-authorised debit, so paying on time is easier.

workzap_build.text: A fee ledger that sends reminders and payment links to parents, with a daily overdue count per centre.

problems.ask_first: Do late payers owe a little each, or do a few families owe a lot?
problems.free_stops: The reminder sequence and overdue rules are in the document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many account references are one month late and how many are longer, so the backlog size is clear.
Give one person one notebook page for overdue account references and a fixed weekly review, so follow-up stays on track.

problems.words: Late pick-up fees are never actually charged
quick_ideas: Check this month's sign-out times against closing time once, so you see how often it happens
Put your late pick-up policy in writing to parents, so charging it isn't a surprise.

workzap_build.text: Late pick-ups noticed from sign-out times and added to the next invoice, under your policy.

problems.ask_first: Do late pick-ups occur most days, or mainly on certain days?
problems.free_stops: How sign-out feeds billing is kept for the document.

extra_ideas.text: Count late sign-outs this week and compare them with fee entries made, so missed charging points are obvious.
Give the closer one handover note for late sign-outs before leaving, so fee entries stop being missed next day.

problems.words: Sign-in sheets are paper and times are often missing
quick_ideas: Ask one staff member to check the sheets at closing, so gaps are fixed the same day
Keep the sheet and a pen at the door, so it's never skipped for lack of one.

workzap_build.text: Digital sign-in and sign-out on a tablet with PINs for adults the centre authorises, and missing times flagged daily.

problems.ask_first: Are times missing mostly at morning drop-off, or at evening pick-up?
problems.free_stops: The sign-in setup and authorisation flow are in the document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many sign-in sheets have missing times at closing this week, so you know which days are slipping most.
Give the closing shift one person responsible for checking the door sheet before lock-up, so missing times get caught that day.

problems.words: Nappies, wipes and formula run out without warning
quick_ideas: Count the supplies store once, so you know what is low
Set a minimum level for each item, so reordering starts before it runs out.

workzap_build.text: A supplies and food register with reorder alerts, and meal counts matched to expected attendance to cut waste.

problems.ask_first: Which item runs out most often: nappies, wipes or formula?
problems.free_stops: The minimum levels and alert setup are kept for the document.

extra_ideas.text: Walk the supplies area once this week and note which items are nearly finished, so surprise runouts stop catching you late.
Give one staff member one notebook page for low-supply notes and a fixed check time, so reordering starts from one place.

problems.words: Cleaning checklists are ticked but I doubt they're done
quick_ideas: Do one spot check against the checklist yourself, so you know the real picture
Make each room's checklist one person's job per shift, so it has an owner.

workzap_build.text: Room checklists completed on a phone with time and a photo of the room (no children in frame), with completion measured per centre.

problems.ask_first: Which cleaning checks worry you most: the toddler rooms, the kitchen, or the bathrooms?
problems.free_stops: How the checks are scheduled and verified is in the document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare the room checklist ticks with what you can actually see at closing once this week, so weak rooms stand out fast.
Make the closer in each room hand the finished checklist to one manager before leaving, so missed cleaning gets chased the same day.

problems.words: Parents message teachers' personal WhatsApp all day
quick_ideas: Give parents one centre number for all messages, so staff phones are left alone
Tell parents the hours that number is answered, so expectations are clear.

workzap_build.text: A centre messaging channel separate from staff phones, with set daily updates and instant replies to common questions.

problems.ask_first: Do parents message teachers mostly during class hours, or in the evenings and weekends?
problems.free_stops: The update templates and reply setup are kept for the document.

extra_ideas.text: Note which teacher phones get parent messages during teaching hours for one week, so you see where interruptions are heaviest.
Give one supervisor the job of collecting parent messages from staff at a set time daily, so teachers stop replying all day.

never_say: Anything on ratios, licensing, subsidy rules, food safety, medication or allergy handling.
Any safeguarding-procedure advice or custody guidance on pick-ups.
Any idea that records a child's name, photo, age, birth date, allergy, health, development or family details.
Help falsifying attendance or enrolment for subsidy claims, or covert recording of staff or children.
Promises about enrolment or full rooms.
Business talk after an injury, illness, missing child or abuse concern; pi points to 1122/15, 999/998 or 911 and the proper authority.

sample_reply.person: The subsidy paperwork is brutal. I sit with the sign-in sheets for two nights every month. Is there any way out of this?
sample_reply.pi:
Sure, this can be sorted, and the first steps are simple.
First, total attendance days per room at the end of each day, so month-end is just adding up.
Second, confirm the claim format once with your provincial programme contact, so nothing is redone.
Workzap would handle this by turning daily attendance into a claim workbook you simply check and submit.

Would you like me to arrange a solution document and quote for you? You're welcome to say no.
